text:
jamie: quick Q — after the terraform secret rename yesterday, HPA stopped reacting to burst traffic on the worker API pods. any ideas?

sophia: saw that too on staging. HPA metrics view shows no cpu/memory spikes, but custom metrics (requests-per-second) jumps. are we still shipping custom-metrics adapter?

ryan: infra-ci reported a failed rollout for `metrics-server` in the post-rename pipeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/892 checks. infra-bot: `metrics-server` deployment restart due to RBAC token mount path mismatch. :grimacing:

anita: uh — the terraform var rename changed `k8s_metrics_secret` -> `k8s_metrics_sa_secret`. the adapter expects the old secret name. PR 893 is queued to update the adapter deployment to use the new secret. quick workaround: patch the HPA to use CPU target while we fix adapter.

jamie: can you paste the patch? I can run it on prod-ish cluster for a quick mitigation.

sophia: run this to set a short-term CPU target (will make pods scale on CPU instead of custom metric):

```bash
kubectl patch hpa worker-api -n prod --type='merge' -p '{"spec": {"metrics": [{"type": "Resource", "resource": {"name": "cpu", "target": {"type": "Utilization", "averageUtilization": 50}}}]}}'
```

ryan: FYI the root cause is two-fold: (1) adapter not mounting secret due to name mismatch, (2) cluster-autoscaler / HPA interplay — CA autoscale threshold is too conservative so nodes weren't added fast enough for pod bursts. We should loosen CA scale-up delay and ensure the adapter is healthy.

anita: Agreed. Proposed config changes in terraform:

- update `var.k8s_metrics_secret` usage to `var.k8s_metrics_sa_secret` across module `monitoring-adapter`
- set `cluster_autoscaler.scale_up_delay` from `2m` -> `30s` for bursty services (opt-in via label)
- add note to `infra/README.md` about secret renames and rolling restarts

jamie: does the CA change risk flapping? we don't want churn.

sophia: if we make it opt-in by nodepool label (e.g., `autoscale.burst=true`) only apply to worker pools running stateless low-latency APIs, risk is limited. plus keep `scale_down_delay` unchanged.

ryan: also add an extra check in the pipeline: after terraform apply, run `kubectl rollout status deploy/metrics-server -n kube-system` and fail if not ready. infra-ci can add that step (PR suggestion in https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/894).

infra-ci: automated note: I can add the rollout check as a post-apply job. Would you like a failing or a warning policy?

anita: failing for metrics infra, warning for peripheral things. metrics-server is critical for HPA.

jamie: thanks — I'll apply the HPA patch now as a temporary fix, and wait for PR 893/894 to land. can someone once PR lands trigger a staging run and ping here? @ryan @sophia

ryan: will do. also plan to run a synthetic spike test (wrk) after staging is green to validate CA reacts within 60s.

sophia: note for runbook: if HPA metrics go missing after infra changes, check:
1) secret name in Deployment (metrics adapter)
2) adapter logs `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/custom-metrics-adapter`
3) metrics API availability `kubectl get --raw "/apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1"`
4) CA events `kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/cluster-autoscaler`

jamie: awesome. tagging this thread as follow-up needed. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Incident note created: #INF-2026-07 — HPA custom metric outage; linked PRs 893, 894; assignees: anita, ryan.
